Create an Rmarkdown document called "example.Rmd" that contains the following:

```{r echo=FALSE}
require(nlme)
mod <- lme(distance~age, ~age|Subject, data=Orthodont)
summary(mod)
```

Then:

library(knitr)
library(markdown)
knit("example.Rmd") #converts the Rmarkdown to regular markdown
markdownToHTML("example.md") #converts the regular markdown to html


The html output is:


## Loading required package: nlme


## Linear mixed-effects model fit by REML
##  Data: Orthodont 
##     AIC   BIC logLik
##   454.6 470.6 -221.3
## 
## Random effects:
##  Formula: ~age | Subject
##  Structure: General positive-definite, Log-Cholesky parametrization
##             StdDev Corr  
## (Intercept) 2.3270 (Intr)
## age         0.2264 -0.609
## Residual    1.3100       
## 
## Fixed effects: distance ~ age 
##             Value Std.Error DF t-value p-value
## (Intercept) 16.76    0.7752 80  21.620       0
## age          0.66    0.0713 80   9.265       0
##  Correlation: 
##     (Intr)
## age -0.848
## 
## Standardized Within-Group Residuals:
##       Min        Q1       Med        Q3       Max 
## -3.223106 -0.493761  0.007317  0.472151  3.916033 
## 
## Number of Observations: 108
## Number of Groups: 27

HTH

Julin

  • automatically generate LaTeX tables of lme model results [1 Update]
 automatically generate LaTeX tables of lme model results
    Bonnie Dixon <bonnie...@gmail.com> Jun 14 04:36PM -0700  

    Dear D-RUG friends;
     
    I am using the function, lme, within the package, nlme, to create mixed
    effects models. I would like to include tables of the model results in PDF
    documents that I create with R Markdown. Does anyone know of a simple way
    to generate a LaTeX table of lme model results? You would think there
    would be a package that does this, but so far my googling of the topic has
    revealed that neither xtable, nor stargazer, has a method for lme objects.
    texreg does handle lme objects, but the resulting table does not include
    the random effects, which are an essential part of the results.
     
    Here is the closest I have come to a solution:
     
    require(nlme)
    require(texreg)
    mod <- lme(distance~age, ~age|Subject, data=Orthodont)
    texreg(mod)
     
    When run in an R Markdown document to generate a PDF, this results in a
    nice table, but it is not complete because it doesn't include the variance
    components of the random effects. If anyone knows of a way to get texreg
    to include random effects, or a different way of doing this, please let me
    know. Thanks!
     
    Bonnie

messages.author: f8f554f3c8aec296
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Digest for davis-rug@googlegroups.com - 1 update in 1 topic
parts:
Bonnie, 

While that example is helpful for printing the whole summary it sounds like you want a latex table that includes both fixed and random. 
There's no quick function for this (perhaps because there's not a standard format??). But,  `VarCorr` extracts the ranef, and some poking around yields: 

<snip>
(s <- summary(mod))

## assuming you want the tables after Fixed effects and Random effects:
## but sounds like you already have the fixef table

(re <- VarCorr(mod)) # prints the ranef table you want
str(re) # str is a friend
re.df <- as.data.frame(re[1:3, 1:3])

library(xtable)
xtable(re.df)
</snip>

Cheers, 
Jaime

<snip>

</snip>
is an array with your desired fixed effects table. So it should be possible to combine these two tables to make one, sparse data frame and apply eg xtable
